title: Succinct Certificates for Exact Mahalanobis Rerandomization Acceptance Probabilities
banked_reason: D-0.5 NO-PASS: no supported field-scale capability distinction survived three revisions of the bounded workflow or the succinct-certificate pivot.
gap_reasons: the proposed few-type certified-workflow integration has no verified field-scale capability distinction from exact rerandomization and exact-inference systems beyond the bounded local comparisons
the audit establishes no consequential capability distinction for the highly structured rank-one radix family
it does not inspect the certified exact-counting/proof-checking literature needed to support a field-scale novelty claim
proof_attempt_summary: Angle 0 refined the grouped sparse-counting workflow through three reviewed versions, repairing its benchmark and certificate contracts but never showing a field-scale capability beyond existing exact systems. Angle 1 replaced the full histogram with a succinct paired-radix certificate, but only separated checking from unpruned occupancy enumeration on an artificial rank-one family; no practical growing class, optimized-counting separation, or matched executable audit could be supported. A future re-raise needs those three pieces as new evidence rather than another revision of either exhausted proposal.
tldr: Can an exact Mahalanobis rerandomization acceptance probability be independently certified from a polynomial-size proof when the number of covariate types grows and full coefficient output is exponential? This proposal investigates a paired radix family with singular covariance, arbitrary rational thresholds, and a locally checked signed-digit table. It seeks a sound and cap-conditional complete certificate for exact design probabilities and Fisher-resolution decisions, plus a matched audit of existing exact systems.
gap: Exact assignment enumeration and score-count dynamic programming are established, but the supplied audit did not locate a deterministic, locally checkable succinct certificate for a rational Mahalanobis acceptance count when an explicit score table is exponentially large. That is a bounded search gap, not a published open problem.
fill: Establish the exact metric reduction, signed-digit certificate soundness, cap-conditional completeness, polynomial versus occupancy separation, and an output-barrier theorem, then test the output-equivalent adapters against named exact methods.
